criteria: The intended glazed ceramic appearance must be demonstrated using the actual exported channels under controlled PBR lighting; flat channel swatches alone are insufficient.

Repeat boundaries preserve the tile rhythm.
Neutral tangent-space normal and zero plane height are intentional.
Fine tiles change density while matte changes roughness only.

observations: Two opaque balanced colors; eight tiles per axis in default, sixteen in fine-tiles.
No extra repeated-edge band visible in 2x2 previews.
Roughness swatch rises from 43 to 112 in matte; baseColor is unchanged.
Actual exported PNGs drive the same Blender Principled BRDF in all three controlled scenes; input hashes match the unchanged baseline.
Default and fine-tiles show narrow softbox highlights and a clearer reflected sample pattern; matte has broader, softer reflections with identical baseColor, normal and height inputs.
Sphere curvature and rounded sample backing are consumer geometry. No grout, bevel, noise, coat layer or surface microstructure was generated in Mixture.
The 512-sample Cycles frames retain slight sampling grain; this is scene-render noise, not a generated texture feature.
